name: Faith Technologies, Inc.
headquarters: Menasha, Wisconsin, USA (manufacturing: Appleton and Little Chute WI, Olathe KS; El Paso TX, Opelika AL, Pittsboro IN and Monroe LA plants announced November 2025 to August 2026)
founded: 1972 (Town & Country Electric, Appleton WI; SKC Electric 1980; bought back from Encompass Services and re-formed as Faith Technologies, Inc. in October 2002)
employees: ~4,600 (December 2025, per Insight on Business); company boilerplate ranged from 'more than 4,500' (November 2025) to 'more than 6,000 team members' (May–July 2026); 3,735 at year-end 2024 (Deloitte Wisconsin 75 book)

ownership.notes: Wisconsin business corporation (DFI F033755) registered with SAM as a Subchapter S corporation; the company's only ownership statement is that the 2002 buyback from Encompass put the business 'under team member ownership'. Department of Labor Form 5500 filings (EIN 41-2065665) show a 401(k), a 401(a) and a welfare plan and no ESOP — the retirement plans hold no employer securities — so the structure is direct shareholding by employees (about 80 shareholders in 2004; current breadth undisclosed), not an ESOP. Not on the NCEO Employee Ownership 100.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Faith Technologies Incorporated (FTI) is a merit-shop electrical contractor whose data-centre business is now the fastest-growing in EC&M's Top 50 — 2025 electrical sales of USD 2.28bn, up 62.6%, ninth in the September 2026 ranking — and whose defining bet is industrialised construction: five new Excellerate prefabrication plants of about 500,000 sq ft each announced between November 2025 and August 2026 (El Paso, Opelika, Pittsboro, Monroe and an Olathe expansion, roughly USD 550m of announced capex), feeding modular electrical buildings and power modules to hyperscale sites. BACKGROUND. Menasha, Wisconsin; founded 1972 as Town & Country Electric; privately held under direct employee shareholding since the 2002 buyback (an S corporation, not an ESOP, per DOL filings). Three brands: Faith Technologies (electrical contracting — design-build, medium-voltage, critical power), Excellerate (manufacturing — modular electrical buildings, e-houses, trestles, skids; from April 2026 an OEM brand, Excellerate Products, selling UL 891 switchboards, a 2 MW power module and the eSkid EV-charging skid) and EnTech Solutions (microgrids, solar, storage, EV charging). The company states more than 950 MW of greenfield data-centre work and 1.5 GW of modular solutions delivered over ten years; the one named hyperscale campus is Meta's Lebanon, Indiana build with Turner and Mortenson. ABC ranked it the No. 1 high-tech/data-centre contractor by hours worked in 2025 and 2026; ENR placed it 32nd among specialty contractors on 2023 revenue of USD 1.06bn. Collection gap: no company-published revenue, margin or backlog exists — every figure above is a ranker's; the Excellerate OEM line has no named third-party buyer in any reachable source, which is why the dossier files FTI as an EPC and not a supplier.
ecosystemRole: We assess FTI as a build-segment electrical contractor on the record — ENR type code E, EC&M's Top 50 Electrical Contractors, ABC's No. 1 high-tech/data-centre contractor — that has moved further than any peer except Rosendin toward owning its own factory: Excellerate's plants pre-build the electrical rooms, trestles and power modules FTI's crews then install. The category is `epc`, not `supplier`, because every revenue figure is contracting revenue and every reachable description of the factories' output routes it to FTI's own project sites; Excellerate Products (OEM, April 2026) has standalone buyer terms and a national sales manager but no named outside purchaser, so the adjacent in-hall-power seat is withheld until one is recorded.

productsAndServices.name: Data-centre electrical construction (Faith Technologies brand)
productsAndServices.description: Design-build and design-assist electrical delivery for hyperscale, colocation and enterprise data centres: medium-voltage service and distribution, generator and switchboard installation, UPS and battery systems, overhead cable trestles between buildings, and Level 1–5 commissioning support. The company states that over the past ten years it has 'provided more than 950 megawatts in greenfield data center construction sites and delivered more than 1.5 gigawatts in modular solutions'. Merit-shop (open-shop) labour; ABC ranked FTI the No. 1 high-tech/data-centre contractor by hours worked in both 2025 and 2026.
highlights: Meta Lebanon, Indiana — named with Turner and Mortenson on Meta's 1,500-acre, roughly 4 million sq ft, more than USD 10bn campus (1 GW at completion per Construction Dive; first phase early 2028); FTI's stated role is near-site manufacturing and integration facilities, two warehouse hubs and 'millions of labor hours with an industrialized approach'

Overhead conveyance trestles for a confidential client 'across several states' — low-, medium- and high-voltage cabling carried on modularised 50-foot sections fabricated at Excellerate, replacing underground duct banks

Atlanta colocation operator (relationship since 2014): USD 3.25m electrical-room build-out — four 600 kW generators, two 4,000 A generator switchboards, a new 4,000 A utility service; 'the client purchased equipment and FTI stored and installed it'
Medium-voltage self-perform: 'tens of thousands of MV terminations annually', with a 3M cable-preparation robot used for terminations and cutbacks

EC&M 2026 Top 50 Electrical Contractors: No. 9 on 2025 sales of USD 2,283,638,907, up 62.64% — the largest growth rate in the top ten; ENR 2024 Top 600 Specialty Contractors No. 32 (type E) on 2023 revenue of USD 1,063.6m
productsAndServices.positioning: Against Rosendin (EC&M No. 2, USD 5.5bn) and EMCOR's electrical segment (No. 3, USD 5.1bn), FTI is less than half the size but growing faster; against M.C. Dean and MMR it competes for the same hyperscale electrical packages. Its differentiation is the share of labour it moves into its own factories ('more than 50% of project labor' for modular data-centre power, per the company) and a merit-shop labour model that ABC's hours-based rankings reward; it lacks the mechanical scope EMCOR brings and the owner-reported MW record Rosendin publishes.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct contracts with owners and with general contractors (Turner and Mortenson at Meta Lebanon; DPR on the Clarksville battery plant); design-build, design-assist and EPC under a single contract
productsAndServices.roadmap: Meta Lebanon first phase online early 2028; four 500,000 sq ft Excellerate plants opening mid-2026 (El Paso) to spring 2027 (Monroe) to feed data-centre modular work; ENR 2026 Top 600 (publishes 2026-10-22) is the next independent revenue read

productsAndServices.name: Excellerate — industrialised construction (engineer-to-order)
productsAndServices.description: FTI's manufacturing arm since 2014: modular electrical buildings (MEBs) for data centres, e-houses housing MV and LV switchgear and motor-control equipment, skidded substations and distribution, overhead trestle sections, electrical assemblies (hangers, conduit, duct banks, underground racks) and mechanical pipe skids. Commissioning through Level 3 is done in the factory, 'potentially up to Level 5'. Plants: Appleton and Little Chute (385,000 sq ft, opened November 2023) in Wisconsin, Olathe KS (roughly 442,000 + 438,000 sq ft, with a 2.16 MW rooftop array), and five announcements in ten months — El Paso TX (500,000 sq ft, USD 81.6m, operations mid-2026), Opelika AL (USD 79m, former JoAnn distribution centre), Pittsboro IN (500,000 sq ft, USD 67.5m), Monroe LA (500,000 sq ft, USD 80.5m, spring 2027) and an Olathe expansion backed by USD 239.8m of industrial revenue bonds (about 1.4–1.5 million sq ft, 1,153 jobs over ten years).
highlights: Every state economic-development release routes the factories' output to 'hyperscale data centers' or 'large-scale infrastructure projects'; Inside Indiana Business ties Pittsboro to FTI's own Meta Lebanon role
Modular data-centre power: 'shifts more than 50% of project labor' to the factory; MEBs 'eliminating the majority of on-site electrical work' (company)
Duct-bank prefabrication case: '67% of labor hours offsite', 'installs three times faster', roughly USD 1m saved per 10,000 hours moved (company)
Crypto-mining e-house spec: 40-ft containers at 2.5 MVA, 415/240 VAC, three 1,200 A I-LINE mains and 28 Powerlink panelboards per container (Schneider Electric / Square D product names)
About USD 550m of announced plant capex and roughly 1,950 announced jobs between November 2025 and August 2026 (derived from the state releases)
productsAndServices.positioning: The closest analogue in the covered set is Rosendin's Modular Power Solutions; FTI's plant footprint (seven sites built or announced) is the larger of the two by announced square footage. Unlike a merchant OEM, every reachable description routes Excellerate output to FTI's own installations.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Integrated with FTI's project contracts; engineer-to-order quotes for third parties are offered on the website but no outside buyer is named
targetSegments: FTI's own data-centre and industrial projects
Owners wanting off-site commissioned electrical rooms
productsAndServices.roadmap: El Paso operational mid-2026; Pittsboro and Opelika 2026–27; Monroe spring 2027; Olathe three-building expansion approved August 2026

productsAndServices.name: Excellerate Products — the OEM line (UL 891 LV switchboards, Power Module 2 MW, eSkid)
productsAndServices.category: Manufactured products · launched as an OEM brand April 2026
productsAndServices.description: Standardised, configure-to-order products sold under standalone buyer terms (net 30, FOB origin, title retained until paid, 12 months from installation or 18 from shipment warranty, aftermarket parts by catalogue). UL 891 LV switchboards in 2,000/3,000/4,000 A frames, indoor or outdoor, 'works with industry-leading breaker brands'; the Power Module 2 MW, which 'consolidates multiple electrical components including integrated UPS systems, switchboards and batteries into a single, scalable power distribution module' with SCADA/PLC/HMI monitoring, walk-in serviceability and 2N options; and the eSkid, an above-ground EV-charging skid powering up to eight DC fast chargers (1 MW today, 2.5 MW planned). Jon Branson is VP and GM of Products; Matt Smith National Sales Manager.
highlights: OEM launch 2026-04-07: 'First to market is the Excellerate Products UL891 LV Switchboards', shown at Data Center World (booth 1220)
Power Module 2 MW: UL 891, NEC 2023, NEMA 3R, ISO 14001 and RoHS; '30% shorter lead times'; voltage, ampacity, enclosure and monitoring configurable
The company's NOC now monitors 'products we manufacture as an original equipment manufacturer (OEM)' alongside its installations

Collection gap: no named third-party buyer, order, shipment, UL file number or distributor appears in any first-party or third-party source as of October 2026 — the line is intended for merchant sale but there is no evidence a merchant sale has occurred
productsAndServices.positioning: Enters the prefabricated power-module space occupied by Schneider Electric, Vertiv and Eaton's Fibrebond and by Rosendin's MPS; FTI's module integrates other OEMs' UPS, breakers and batteries rather than its own ('we partner with leading OEMs'). Until a buyer is recorded this is a product line in the catalogue sense, not in the revenue sense.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct sales team (National Sales Manager), quote or order by contact form; volume pricing offered; e-commerce parts catalogue referenced in the terms
targetSegments: Colocation and high-density data-centre power rooms
Industrial, healthcare and utility switchboard buyers
productsAndServices.roadmap: eSkid capacity to 2.5 MW (company); first named external order is the trigger that would move FTI's segment role (see ecosystemRole)

strategyRead: 1. (High confidence) We assess that FTI's strategy is to win hyperscale electrical packages on labour certainty: by moving half or more of the hours into its own factories it can promise schedule on sites where craft supervision, not equipment, is the constraint — the same bottleneck EMCOR's chief executive names. Basis: five 500,000 sq ft plants and an Olathe expansion announced in ten months, all described by the host states as serving hyperscale data centres.

2. (High confidence) We assess that the correct category is electrical contractor, not supplier. Basis: every revenue figure is contracting revenue (ENR type E, EC&M, ABC electrical); every reachable description of Excellerate output routes it to FTI's own sites; Excellerate Products has buyer terms and a sales manager but, as of October 2026, no named outside purchaser. The decision flips on the first named third-party order.

3. (Moderate confidence) We assess that the 62.6% growth in 2025 electrical sales is largely one hyperscaler's programme. Basis: Meta Lebanon is the only named hyperscale customer, the Pittsboro plant is tied to it by Indiana press, and the company's own project list names no other hyperscale campus; a Microsoft or Amazon attribution exists only on a jobs aggregator. Concentration risk is therefore high and unmeasurable.

4. (Moderate confidence) We assess that the merit-shop model is both the growth engine and the ceiling. Basis: ABC's hours-based rankings put FTI first in data centres while EC&M's revenue table puts it ninth — FTI sells craft hours cheaply relative to union peers, which suits owners in right-to-work Southern and Midwestern markets but limits it in Northern Virginia and California, where the covered union contractors dominate.

5. (Moderate confidence) We assess that direct employee shareholding in an S corporation, rather than an ESOP, leaves succession and plant financing dependent on retained earnings, bank debt and municipal bonds (the USD 239.8m Olathe IRBs). Basis: DOL filings show no employer securities in any plan; the company has published no revenue, margin or balance sheet since 2002. A capital event — outside investor, ESOP conversion or sale — is the structural indicator to watch.

6. (Low confidence) We assess that the 2 MW power module is positioned as a colocation product that will first ship on FTI's own jobs. Basis: the page calls it 'proven, productized' without a reference site; the module integrates other OEMs' UPS and breakers; FTI's NOC already monitors OEM units. Treat any 'deployed' claim as unverified until a buyer or site is named.

relationships.note: Named by Meta as a delivery partner, with Turner and Mortenson, on the Lebanon, Indiana campus.
relationships.context: Meta's 2026-02-11 announcement lists 'Mortenson, Turner Construction, Faith Technologies' among its partners on the roughly 4 million sq ft, more than USD 10bn Lebanon campus (1 GW at completion per Construction Dive; first phase early 2028). FTI's own recruiting page describes its role as near-site manufacturing and integration facilities, two warehouse hubs and millions of labour hours. Meta does not state FTI's trade scope; it is implied by FTI's business. The Pittsboro plant is connected to this campus by Indiana press.

Meta and Mortenson both name Turner and Faith Technologies together on the Lebanon campus; Turner is the general contractor appointed by Meta per World Construction Network. FTI's position is the electrical trade and modular-manufacturing partner alongside the two GCs.
